Subject: Pricing band questions for Azure private offer

Hi Markus —

Thanks for the deck yesterday. Procurement asked me to get clarity on two items before we share a formal PO: 1) how the banded list pricing maps to the reseller passback (we need a worked example), and 2) whether committed volume can be split across regions without changing the band thresholds.

On item 1, a simple waterfall example would be perfect — BrightLabs needs to show finance how list price moves to net revenue after passbacks and distributor fees. On item 2, our Azure footprint is 70% us-west, 30% eu-west. If we keep one global commit, will channels get credited by region or by global consumption?

Also, can you confirm if early-adopter credits would reduce the list price or be treated as a rebate post-invoice? We prefer the latter for revenue recognition.

Appreciate a worked spreadsheet if you have it.

Best,
Lara
Head of Cloud Procurement
BrightLabs

Hi Lara —

Thanks for the clear asks. I've looped Ben (channel economics) and Irene (marketplace ops) to answer both parts. Quick answers up front:
- Waterfall: passback is applied at invoice-level and is a post-list rebate; we'll send a worked example that shows list -> partner gross -> passback -> Redwood net.
- Regional split: commits can be regionalized, but our private offer mechanics default to global aggregation unless you request region-anchored tiers. There are trade-offs for channel crediting — we'll detail them.
- Early-adopter credits: treated as a rebate (post-invoice) by default; if finance needs a different treatment we can explore swap language on the PO.

Attaching a model (first pass) that lays out three band scenarios and the passback waterfall. Ben: could you review the assumptions (15% distributor fee, reseller passback tiers at 10/7/4%) and confirm if those look doable for the BrightLabs channel partner structure? Irene: can you validate whether Azure private offer will allow per-region commit segmentation or if we need to submit separate POs per region?

Next step: Mark Lara's procurement preference (rebate post-invoice) and we'll iterate.

Thanks,
Markus
Senior Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Markus / Lara —

Reviewed the spreadsheet. A few notes on assumptions and an alternate waterfall that may be more illustrative for BrightLabs finance:

Assumptions I used (call these out in the sheet):
- List price per token/unit = $0.020 (for baseline band)
- Distributor fee (up-front flow) = 15% of list (paid to distributor). This is a pass-through deduction before reseller passback.
- Reseller passback tiers (by net ARR to channel): Tier A: >= $1.5M -> 10%; Tier B: $750k-$1.5M -> 7%; Tier C: <$750k -> 4%
- Early-adopter credit = one-time post-invoice rebate applied in quarter 1 at $50k

Worked example (sheet 'Example_A'):
- List invoice: $2,000,000
- Distributor fee (15%): $300,000 -> leaves $1,700,000
- Reseller passback (Tier A @10%): $170,000 -> leaves Redwood recognized revenue $1,530,000
- Accounting treatment: BrightLabs sees $2,000,000 gross, but net paid after passbacks/credits is lower — finance prefers post-invoice rebate to keep gross list intact.

On regional commits: Azure private offer accepts a single global commit, but channel credits are calculated at distribution settlement time. If you want channel uplift/crediting by region we recommend separate region-anchored POs — operationally heavier but cleaner for partner compensation. Irene, can ops support a split-PO for BrightLabs if they choose that?

Lara, I also added a sensitivity tab that shows how moving 10% of consumption from us-west to eu-west affects the tiering and which band you'd land in. Let us know the expected monthly run-rate and we can tune thresholds.

Cheers,
Ben
Director, Channel Economics
Redwood Inference

Hi all —

Operational confirmation from marketplace side:
1) Azure private offers support a single global commit by default. We can request region-anchored commit tiers but that requires separate private offers per region (Azure limitation). BrightLabs would need to accept three PO PDFs (one per region) or we can create a parent PO plus region sub-POs — legal prefers separate docs.

2) Passback mechanics: Azure will process the private offer invoice against the list price we submit. Distributor/reseller passbacks are handled off-platform as contractually-agreed rebates (we remit to the distributor/reseller). For settlement clarity, we provide a monthly reconciliation file showing list invoice, distributor fee, passback amounts, and Redwood net.

3) Next ops steps if BrightLabs wants region-split: confirm region names + committed $/month per region; procurement should approve separate PO templates. If you want us to try aggregated commit but regional channel credits, expect more manual settlement and potential lag in month-to-month partner crediting.

I've attached a PO draft with language for rebate treatment (clause 4.2) — please review and flag any redlines.

Thanks,
Irene
Sr. Marketplace Operations
Redwood Inference
